item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2042…
item.description: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2042 date comes from the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance. That was wrong. The Port's 2017 staff report (Item 9B, p.7) puts the Schedule of Performance in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) between the Port and the developer, which is a different agreement from the Development Agreement between the City and the developer. The report says the developer must complete phase 3 within approximately 25 years of project approval, but it never states the year 2042; 2042 is Pier & Point's own arithmetic (2017 plus 25 years). It stays labelled a legal outside date, not an expected completion. Source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf.

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space: The 2042 date shown for the waterfront parks is only…
item.description: The 2042 date shown for the waterfront parks is only an outermost bound: Pier & Point's arithmetic for the final-phase outside date in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA)'s Schedule of Performance, which is separate from the City's Development Agreement. It applies only to the parks the Port lists in Phase 3 (Waterfront Terrace and Waterfront Promenade 2), not to the Phase 1 parks. It remains labelled a legal outside date, not a forecast. Source: Port of San Francisco, Item 9B: Pier 70 Mixed-Use Project approvals, Sep 22, 2017 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Item 11A: Pier 70 28-Acre Site Project update, Aug 7, 2026 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf).

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space: The 2042 date on this record was drawn as an expected…
item.description: The 2042 date on this record was drawn as an expected completion. The Port's 2017 staff report calls it an outside date in the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance (Phase 3 within approximately 25 years of approval), not a construction schedule. It is now labelled a legal deadline and no longer moves this record's status on the map or the timeline. Source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf.

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space: The Phase 1 park schedule is described as tolled by…
item.description: The Phase 1 park schedule is described as tolled by the down market delay (extended to December 26, 2026, Port Item 11A) rather than lapsed, with the 2042 whole-project date kept only as a soft original outside date. The map notes now say the Port's SUD Land Use Plan labels separate open-space segments, and no longer say no source draws a boundary between them or that the space has no Assessor lot. The sea-level-rise fact now quotes the 2026 report's 'mitigations' wording and the 2018 release's future tense ('will be raised', 'nearly nine feet'); 'since 2022' was dropped from the Port's statement; the Slipways Commons plan is no longer credited to private firms the figure does not name; the earlier entries for the Sep 26, 2017 approval and the Dec 8, 2020 agenda item were reworded; and the Aug 11, 2026 Port Commission minutes now back the informational hearing. Source: Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 11A staff report, 2026-08-07 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 9B staff report, 2017-09-22 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Pier 70 SUD Land Use Plan, 2018-03-13 (https://sfport.com/files/2021-11/pier_70_sud_land_use_plan.pdf); Port of San Francisco, news release, 2018-05-10 (https://www.sfport.com/about/news/new-life-pier-70-historic-shipyard-construction-begins-expansive-waterfront-district); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 12B and Resolution 20-07, 2020-02-11 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Documents/Item%2012B%20Pier%2070%20Parcels%20E2%20and%20A.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Port Commission minutes, 2026-08-11 (https://www.sfport.com/media/11558/download?inline).

item.title: Planned · Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space: Port reports that the balance of Phase 1… (Aug 7, 2026)
item.description: Port reports that the balance of Phase 1, 'largely comprised of the Phase 1 parks and open space,' will be built 'on a schedule that coincides with the delivery of adjacent vertical development,' which 'has not moved forward' because of pandemic-driven office-vacancy increases, construction-cost escalation and higher financing costs (Aug 7, 2026). item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space: No completion date is sourced for these parks (~2042)
item.description: No completion date is sourced for these parks. 2042 is shown only as the outermost bound: Pier & Point's arithmetic for the DDA's Phase 3 outside date (approximately 25 years after Project approval; the Port's report states no calendar year), which Table A (p.8) applies only to the parks it lists under Phase 3 (Waterfront Terrace and Waterfront Promenade WP-2). The Phase 1 parks' DDA deadlines are tied to adjacent buildings, have been tolled by the down market delay (extended to December 26, 2026) and the adjacent vertical development remains paused (~2042). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2017-09-22; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space: Port Commission meeting scheduled to act… (Sep 26, 2017)
item.description: Port Commission meeting scheduled to act on the DDA terms (the Port's Item 9B memo is dated Sep 22, 2017, before the meeting, so it cannot confirm the vote; the Port's Aug 2026 report says the Pier 70 Special Use District was approved 'In 2017'). The terms the memo proposes: parks must be completed 12-18 months after completion of adjacent buildings; the Port Commission must approve the schematic design of each park after review by a design advisory committee; parks are owned and controlled by the Port (Sep 26, 2017). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2017-09-22; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
